ratings_why.fun: The reset has three real exits (gold, lending to other tribes, Waxing on purpose) and Full Moon seating is a puzzle, but a few cards are flat bodies and the two-up, two-down cycle can feel like waiting.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 because every buy is priced by shelf life against a clock you can push, and losing light is itself a resource; no tribe today has buffs that expire on a schedule.

verdict_why: The core is strong; Leveret's target and Sister Silverpenny's timing need clear wording, which is a real if small fix.

points.text: "The first unit in front of it" can mean two diagonal slots, and a front-row Leveret has none. Say which slot, or use "the unit behind/in front of it with the most Attack".

Sister Silverpenny's copy ends "until the New Moon": does a copied New Moon text (Old Wat, Courting Jack) fire at that New Moon? And with Dame Waxwell, does the second Full Moon trigger copy again? Rule both.
The Fast Moon's only lasting payoff is The Moon-Scour's counter. A Hare that counts New Moons this game (lights gone out) would give the Wax engine a second, different reason to race the clock.
Dusk-Runner is a flat body for the dark turns. If it fought with a share of the light lost at the last New Moon, it would tie the weak turns into the reset instead of patching them.
Waxing at End of Turn to fight at the Full Moon, versus Waxing early to start the cycle, is a great choice; make sure the UI shows which phase you will fight in before you commit.

standouts.why: Turns the reset into permanent stats for another tribe's carry; Oozes and Birds make this a cross-tribe combo playground.
Doubling by adjacency plus reading-order resolution makes seating around the Moon-Scour a real puzzle each Full Moon.
A non-Hare in the Hare pool is the loophole to the tribe's own law, and he rewards sitting between your brightest Hares.

weakest.why: A one-off buff body with no tie to the cycle beyond avoiding the New Moon.
Plain stats and Shields on the weak turns; it does one obvious job.
Dead early, and later just a gold drip; it rarely changes a decision.

flags.note: Golden Dame Waxwell with golden Chalk-Cutters multiplies light many times over in one fight; capped by the reset, but worth the owner's eye.
Banks half of a multiplied cycle as permanent stats on non-Hares, which is the one route out of the law.
Which unit is "the first unit in front of it" is not defined.
How copied New Moon and Full Moon triggers behave at the start and end of the copy is not ruled.
